subject: Operationally Safe VPC Schematic — control/data plane stitch and action items
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Harper <emily.harper@acme-corp.com>, infra-ops@nexTier-telecom.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operationally Safe VPC Schematic — initial draft and questions

Hi Emily / infra ops team,

Thanks again for walking the site team through the rack layout yesterday. Attached is a compact reference diagram (vpc-stitch-diagram-v3.png) that pulls together the control-plane/data-plane boundaries we discussed. High-level notes: 

- Control plane (management, versioned API, agent uplinks) sits in a dedicated management VLAN and uses mutual TLS to the Redwood control endpoints.
- Data plane (inference nodes, kv-cache, batching gateway) has no direct outbound access to the public internet. Egress is via an audited NAT gateway in the tenant egress subnet; all traffic is logged.
- A small admin jump host in the management VLAN will be allowed SSH (bastion) with short-lived certs from customer KMS/HSM.

Open questions where we need confirmation from Nextier:
1) Can the site provide Layer‑2 adjacency between the management VLAN and the on‑rack OOB switch for agent heartbeats? If not, we need an alternate UDP handshake route.
2) Is there an existing IPSEC/MPLS path we should prefer for control plane replication, or should we rely on the TLS tunnels over the primary internet uplink?
3) Expected window for maintenance NAT rules changes — do we have a 24h change freeze or can we do a 2h maintenance window?

Action items I propose this week:
- Infra: confirm L2 adjacency / alternative path (infra-ops@nexTier-telecom.com) — due Thu 22 Apr EOD.
- Redwood: produce small-runbook for canary (attached: runbook-canary-checklist.md) and circulate to the security reviewer.
- Ops: stub test plan for KV cache warmup and prefix caching validation.

Emily, can you confirm if your security team needs us to bring any SOC2 evidence for the NAT logging configuration prior to the initial canary?

Thanks,
Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

From: Emily Harper <emily.harper@acme-corp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-ops@nexTier-telecom.com, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 12:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Operationally Safe VPC Schematic — initial draft and questions

Olga — thanks for the diagram and clear list. Quick answers: 

1) L2 adjacency: partial. We can provide a control VLAN that reaches the rack OOB, but there are two intermediary switches that will need a policy update. We will confirm by Thu as requested.
2) Control replication: preference is to put control replication over an MPLS circuit to reduce jitter; backup over TLS on internet uplink is acceptable for failover.
3) Change window: our standard maintenance window is 0200–0400 local (2 hours). For initial canary we can consent to a one-time expanded window of 4 hours with prior notice.

On SOC2 evidence: yes, our security team will want the NAT logging format and retention policy (how long logs are kept and how quickly they are searchable). They asked for sample entries. Can Redwood provide a sample log excerpt and retention SLA?

I'll have infra-ops follow up about L2 policies later today.

—Emily
Emily Harper
Senior Cloud Architect, Acme Corp
em: emily.harper@acme-corp.com
[inline: brief note — prefer MPLS for steady latency]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Paul Turner <paul.turner@edgebridge.io>, Emily Harper <emily.harper@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:33:00 +0200
Subject: Re: Operationally Safe VPC Schematic — control plane replication option + runbook updates

Folks — following up with the control-plane replication design decision:

- If MPLS is available, we should terminate the control replication over the MPLS circuit with BGP session peering directly to the control-plane aggregator. This gives us predictable RTT and avoids small packet prioritization issues.
- For the TLS-over-internet fallback, we'll set a stricter heartbeat (1s) and implement exponential backoff to avoid thundering during partial outages.

I've taken Olga's runbook and added two verification steps:
A) Control-plane auth proof: a simulated agent registration showing the PKI chain (screenshot added to the Drive folder).
B) KV cache warming test: an end-to-end inference call that validates prefix hit rates before golden traffic is diverted to the cluster.

Kimberly — can you handle the SOC2 log sample? We should provide: one week of NAT logs (sample) and the retention statement (we recommend 90 days by default for this configuration).

Paul — any constraints from EdgeBridge side on adding a second BGP adjacency for control replication?

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Principal Infra Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
[attachment: runbook-canary-checklist.md (text/markdown)]

Subject: Re: Operationally Safe VPC Schematic — SOC2 artifacts + next steps

Emily / infra team — attaching a small log excerpt and our retention proposal. Notes: 

- Sample log snippet (first lines):
  2027-04-20T01:12:05Z tenant=acme direction=egress src=10.11.5.22 dst=34.201.12.18 proto=TCP bytes=312 action=allow nat_src=203.0.113.45 session_id=abcd-1234
  2027-04-20T01:12:06Z tenant=acme direction=ingress src=34.201.12.18 dst=10.11.5.22 proto=TCP bytes=980 action=allow session_id=abcd-1234

- Retention: we propose 90 days hot searchable, 365 days archived read-only. If Acme requires less or more, we can flex under contract.
- Next steps:
  1) Infra: confirm L2 policy by Thu EOD (Emily / infra-ops).
  2) EdgeBridge: confirm BGP adjacency feasibility (Paul).
  3) Redwood: schedule canary run for week of 26 Apr; we will target the 0200–0600 window and provide a rollback plan with automated traffic diversion to existing hosted endpoints.

I'll upload the sample log and the retention SLA document to the Drive folder listed in the thread.

Best,
Kimberly
